 6. Study the photograph provided and use it to answer the following questions. (2mks)
 (a) Name the type of photographs show above
 - Ground general view photograph
 (b) Draw a rectangle measuring 8 cm by 5 cm to present the area of the photograph. (1mk)
 Drawing
 (c) (i) Describe the scene in the photograph (4 mks)
 - The main activity is fishing.
 - The fisherman is handling the net and emptying fish into the canoe/boat
 - The fisherman is standing in the canoe as he pull the net.
 - The canoe is stationary and floating on an expansive lake.
 - The sky appears cloudy and it is likely to rain any time. (any 4x1 =4)
 (ii) Name two types of fish caught in the North East Atlantic fishing ground. (2 mks)
 - Mackerel
 - Cod
 (iii) Describe trawling as a fishing method. (4 mks)
 - Trawling method is used to catch fish in the deep sea using large snip or boats known as trawlers.
 - The trawl net which is bag-shaped is attached to a trawler or a snip.
 - The moult of the trawl net is kept open by otter boards or head beams.
 - The upper part of the trawl net is kept a float by corks or floats.
 - Weights are used to keep the lower parts of the net at the sea bed.
 - The trawl nets dragged along the sea bottom by the trawler to trap fish.
 - After sufficient fish is caught, the net is howled into the trawler.
 (d) Explain four factors that have made Japan to be a leading fishing nation (8 mks)
 - Japan is situated on the broad continental shelf. Shallow water helps to produce ideal conditions for
 Plankton growth.
 - It has highly indeed coastline with many bays and sheltered inlets which provide ideal site for fishing
 ports.
 - It is a highly mountainous county with little agriculture. This makes fishing the major source of income.
 - Well developed technology has made deep sea fishing very efficient. This increase the amount of fishing
 caught.
 - There is large market from within the country and abroad.
 - Cool water which have been created by meeting of warm Kuroshio and cool Oyashio current has made it
 possible for growth of Planktons that fish feed on (2x4 =8)
 7. (a)
 i. A part from draining of swamps, give two other methods through which land has been reclaimed in
 Kenya.
 - Irrigation
 - Tsetse fly control
 - Planting of trees/afforestation
 - Flood control
 ii. Give two methods that are used to drain swamps in Kenya.
 - Construction drainage pipes
 - Digging open ditches/canals
 - Pumping out the water. (any 2x1 =2mks)
 (b)
 i. Name two rivers that supply water to the Mwea Tebera irrigation scheme.
 - Thiba river
 - Nyamindi river
 - Murubara
 ii. Explain how the following factors influence the establishment of Mwea Tebera irrigation.
  Topography
 - The gently slopping land makes it possible for water to flow by gravity into and out of the irrigation
 fields.
 - The gently slopping land allows for mechanization which allows large areas to be under cultivation.
 (any 1x2 = 2mks)
  Soils
 - Preserve of black cotton soils which is suitable for cultivation of rice/which retains water for along time.
 (2mks)
  Population
 - The area was originally sparsely populated which enable large areas to be put under cultivation/very few
 people were displaced thus it was cheap to start the scheme.
  Government policy
 - There was need to keep political – detainees busy/use them to provide free labour. This made the colonial
 government to set up the scheme at Mwea where there was a large detention camp.
 (2mks)
 (c)
 i. Name three areas which make up the Zuiden Zee reclamation project in the Netherlands.
 - Market ward
 - South flevoland
 - East Flevoland
 - North-Eastern polders
 - Wieringer meer polder (any 3x1= 3mks)
 ii. Give four differences between land reclamation in Kenya and the Netherlands. (8 mks)
 - In Kenya, the area that is reclaimed is relatively small while the areas reclaimed in Netherlands are large.
 - In Kenya, land is mainly reclaimed from swamps and marginal areas while in Netherlands reclamation is
 from the sea.
 - In Kenya, irrigation is used as a means of reclaiming dry land while irrigation in the Netherlands is used
 to lower salinity of the soil in the reclaimed land.
 - In Kenya the methods of land reclamation are simple, digging canals/ditches to drain water whole in the
 Netherlands methods used are highly advanced like remaining land from the sea/creation of polder.
 - In Kenya, dykes are used to control floods while in Netherlands, dykes protect the reclaimed land from ---
 - by the sea. (any 4x2= 8mks)
 8. (a) What is eco-tourism
 - It is the development and management of tourism whole conserving the environment/it is enjoying what
 nature provide while protecting it. (2mks)
 (b)
 i. Give four tourist attractions found at the coast of Kenya.
 - Marine parks
 - Historical sites
 - Sandy beach/coral reefs/coastal scenery
 - Sunny/warm climate
 - Traditional culture
 - Water sports/beach sports
 - Wildlife
 ii. State five problems associated with tourism in Kenya.
 - Tourism has led to increase in drug abuse.
 - A number of youths especially at the coast have dropped out of school to become tour---/ beach boys/ sex
 workers/ curio sellers.
 - Tourism has led to the spread of disease such as S.T.Is
 - Tourism has led to pollution of environment/ National park/game reserves.
 - Tourism has led encouraged poaching/illegal collection of marine resources.
 - Tourism has led to international terrorism/piracy
 - Erosion of some social values/culture.
 (c) State four ways in which game reserves are of benefits to the communities living near
 them.
 - The game reserves offer employment opportunities to the communities living near them.
 - The management of the game reserves provides social amenities to the communities.
 - The communities are allowed to graze their animals in the game reserve.
 - Access roads to the same reserves benefits the communities.
 - The income earned from the game reserves by the local authority is used to provide services to the communities.
 - Sometimes member of the communities are given meat when animals have been culled.
 - Educational institutions local near the game reserves have easy access for educational ---
 - Increase market for local products (4x1= 4mks)
 (d) Explain three differences between tourism in Kenya and Switzerland.
 - Kenya has tropical climate which is warm and sunny most of the year encouraging sun-bathing whole Switzerland
 has temperature climate with cold water which encourage winter spur.
 - Kenya has varied and beautiful coastal scenery/ Rift valley/volcanic mountains consisting of snow capped
 mountains/glaciated landscape.
 - Kenya being far from Europe gets fewer tourists than Switzerland which is centrally located in Europe.
 - Kenya’s reports of insecurity scare away potential tourists but the reports of peaceful atmosphere in Switzerland
 encourage tourists.
 - Kenya has poorly maintained transport network making it difficult to access tourists sites while in Switzerland
 transport network is sufficient.
 - The training of personnel in tourism industry in Switzerland is more advanced that in Kenya this enabling the
 personnel to provide higher quality service to tourists.
 - The accessibility to financial and services such as the use of credit cards by the tourists in Kenya is limited to large
 urban areas, whereas in Switzerland similar facilities and services are widespread promoting easy transaction to
 tourists.
 - Kenyan’s low purchasing power limits their ability to travel as tourists while Switzerland the high purchasing power
 enables people to travel as tourist.
 - Kenya has coastal beaches while Switzerland has lake sole beaches.
 - In Kenya, animals are found in their natural habitual. While in Switzerland they are found in a zoo.
 - Kenyans are able to speak few languages hence communication with tourists sometimes limited while the diversity
 of languages spoken in Switzerland make it possible for tourists to communicate with ease.
 ii. Your geography class carried out a field study in a game park.
  State two methods the class many have used to collect data.
 - Administering questionnaires.
 - Interviewing/asking questions
 - Taking photograph/video tapping
 - Taking measurements
 - Collecting samples
 - Counting
 - Content analysis
  During the field study the class collected data on the number of tourists ---a game park. State two
 methods the class may have used to present data.
 - Drawing charts
 - Drawing tables
 - Drawing graphs
 9. (a)
 i. Difference between indigenous and exotic forests.
 - Indigenous forests is a forest that is made up of trees which are nature/natural to a county/region while
 exotic forest is a forest that is composed of trees that are alien to a country.
 (2mks)
 ii. Forests marked
 M – Equatorial
 R – Montane
 iii. Factors that lead to depletion of forests in Kenya.
 - The government policy of degazettement has allowed illegal/cultivation and settlement in forests.
 - Increase population of elephants that destroy trees.
 - Prolonged droughts have caused drying up of some trees.
 - Plant disease and pests eg. Aphids destroy parts of forests.
 - Over-exploitation of certain species of trees. (any 3x1=3 mks)
 (b) Factors that favour the growth of natural forests on the slopes of Mt. Kenya.
 - The area receives high rainfall/1000mm-2200mm throughout the year which encourages continuous growth
 of trees.
 - The area has deep fertile volcanic soils that allow the roots to penetrate deep into the ground for proper
 anchorage.
 - The area is a gazette reserve prohibiting cultivation and settlement hence allowing growth of trees.
 - The steep slope discourages settlements thus forests thrive. (any 3x2 =6mks)
 (c) Comparison between forestry in Kenya and Canada under the following subheadings.
 i. Distribution of forests.
 - In Kenya forests are mainly established in the highland regions while in Canada the distribution involves
 both highlands and lowlands.
 ii. Modes of expoitation
 - In Kenya workers are transported to the logging sites daily while in Canada logging involves setting up a
 settlement for workers within a region to be harvested.
 iii. Transport
 - Kenya transportation is mainly by road transport while in Canada transport is mainly by water transport.
 (d)
 i. Factors favouring the development of softwood forests in Canada.
 - Cool to cold climate favours the growth of coniferous trees.
 - Rugged landscape and steep slopes discourages agriculture and settlement hence forests establish themselves
 naturally.
 - Canada has a low population density hence a lot of land for forestry.
 - - Presence of heavy rainfall on the windward slopes of mountain ranges supports tree growth. (any 3x1
 =3mks)
 ii.Measures used to conserve forests in Kenya.
 - Mature trees felled are replaced immediately (re-aforestation)
 - Tree farming is practiced in many parts with the aim of raising trees for future use.
 - Regions which previously were devoid of trees are being planted with trees (afforestation)
 - People are now being encouraged to plant trees and food crops in the same farms/agroforestry.
 - The reduction of wastage eg. The use of waste paper to produce newprint
 - People are required to seek permits if they have to cut trees. This reduces the rate of trees
 felling/unlicensed people do not cut down trees.
 - Forest reserves have been set aside to conserve indigenous species.
 - Forestry dept. of the ministry of natural resource carry out research to produce and distribute seedlings to
 ensure the extension of forests.
 - People are being educated through mass media on the importance of trees. (any 3x2= 3mks)
 10. (a)
 i. Give four factors common to Kenya and the Netherlands that have favoured horticultural farming.
 - Both countries have a varied climatic condition.
 - In both countries horticultural farming is practiced in areas with well drained soils.
 - Both countries sell their horticultural produce in the local and international market.
 - In both countries irrigation is carried out.
 - In both countries large companies/promote organization have invested in horticultural farming.
 - In both countries, green houses are used.
 - Use of advanced technology in both countries.
 - Availability of labour in both countries.
 ii. State three features of horticultural farming in Netherlands.
 - The farms are generally small in size.
 - The farmers use advanced/highly specialized technology techniques of crop production/farmers use green
 house.
 - Most farmers use practice mixed farming.
 - The farms are intensively used.
 - Farming is largely labour intensive.

 June 2009. Use it to answer question. (b)

 i. What was Kenya’s total value of export from horticulture between June 2008.
 - Kshs. 51,200 million/Kshs. 51,200,000,000/51.2 billions (2mks)
 ii. Comment on the trend of the quantity of Kenya’s horticultural exports between june 2008 and
 2009. (3mks)
 - The quantity of exports is fluctuating.
 - The lowest export were in august 2008 and December 2008
 - The highest quantity of export was in March 2009.
 - There was significant drop in the quantity of exports between March and April 2009.
 iii. Using the data provided, draw a simple line graph to present the quantity of kenya’s horticultural
 export.
 - Use a vertical scale of 1 cm to present 500 metric tones
 (c)
 Explain four difficulties that farmers in Kenya experience in marketing horticultural produce.
 -The impassable roads during the rainy season make it difficult for the perishable produce to reach the market
 or time hence causing losses to the farmers.
 - The cost of transporting produce by air is high thus lowering the profit margin.
 - Poor marketing strategies/reliance on middle man who exploit the farmers/farmers incur losses.
 - Low quality produce may lead to rejection/fetch low prices in the market hence making farmers incur
 losses/farmers are demoralized.
 - The farmer face stiff completion from the established/upcoming produces which limit the quantity the
 farmers are able to sell.
 - Stringent quality standards required at the international market increases the cost of production thus lowering
 the profit margin.
 - Fluctuations of the exchange rates cause inconsistencies in the profit margin thus discouraging the farmers.
 - Limited preservation faculties/refrigeration faculties leads to spoilage of the produce hence losses.
 (4x2 =8mks)
